name: Bounce a ping-pong ball into a cup consistently
blurb: A pure calibration skill: the bounce is entirely predictable, so once you find the release point and angle, all you need is repetition.
gear: A cup and a hard table
steps: Set a fixed stance and a fixed distance from the cup, and change nothing else while you learn.
Find the sweet spot: aim for a point about a third of the way from your hand to the cup, and adjust from there.
Use a consistent release — the same fingers, the same height, the same arc every time.
Add a small amount of backspin, which softens the second bounce and keeps the ball in the cup.
Practise 100 throws a day and log your percentage.
Once consistent from one spot, learn to recalibrate quickly for a new distance.
tips: Consistency of everything else is what lets you tune one variable. Change one thing at a time.
A ball that bounces out is usually a flat, spin-free throw. Add backspin.
proof: You hit at least seven out of ten from your practised distance, then adapt to a new table within ten throws.
